title: No Kings movement holds rallies in New York City for midterm voter turnout
seoTitle: New York City No Kings rallies for midterms

tea.why: Protesters opposed the administration's policies and actions, which they described as authoritarian and billionaire-first.
tea.want: They aimed to boost early voting and turnout for the upcoming midterm elections.
tea.changed: Oct 17: More than 200 people gathered at the James A. Farley Post Office building for a rally.

summary: The grassroots No Kings movement shifted its tactics from street protests to voter mobilization events across the United States, including at least 13 events across the five boroughs of New York City. The coalition organized the nationwide events to increase voter turnout for the midterm elections. More than 200 people gathered on the steps of the historic James A. Farley Post Office building in Manhattan on Saturday afternoon, carrying signs and encouraging community members to make a plan to vote early. Speakers and participants highlighted the importance of defending the Constitution and participating in the democratic process ahead of the elections. The movement was originally orchestrated by the 50501 Movement to reject perceived authoritarianism and militarization.
response: No official response reported in the sources.
